reason: Both implementations passed the supplied invoice-audit behavior and relocation checks. The Veritas follow-up was quicker in the recorded phase timings and runs without Python; Python has much faster measured launches and avoids shipping a large runtime. The paired evidence does not justify a clear language winner for this small task.
observed_user_benefit: Veritas produced a relocatable Python-free command and applied the vendor-filter change quickly; Python delivered the same core audit with a standard-library script and roughly 55 ms median process time in this run.
material_regressions: The installed Veritas CLI rejected bare `veritas --help` with exit 1; the builder recovered using the shipped usage note and product reference.

The paired Python source accepts signed cents as credit amounts, while the Veritas source rejects negative amounts. The brief does not define whether credits are valid, so this is a real behavior difference but not a failed stated acceptance case.

The Veritas app package measured 12,881,497 bytes, including a 12,824,672-byte runtime; the Python implementation instead requires CPython 3.14.7 to be present. No third-party Python packages were installed.

Python timing records disagree on the follow-up boundary: the normalized report records 69.777 seconds, while the detailed self-report records 57.250 seconds. Treat phase timings as builder records, not a controlled cross-language benchmark.
